note: FROZEN codec (ontos-codec-v1), normatively specified in docs/spec/ontos-codec.md; the byte mapping is immutable and any change ships as a new version. Atom(b)=0x00||uvarint(len(b))||b; Tuple(vs)=0x01||uvarint(arity)||encode(child)...; uvarint=shortest-form unsigned LEB128 over the u64 domain. Bytes hand-computed from the spec + verified green across go/rs/ts. The uvarint integer domain is now PINNED to u64 (spec §3.1): a uvarint encoding a value >=2^64 is cross-core `uvarint_overflow` (pinned below); a value within u64 but exceeding a particular core's native length type is an impl-local resource limit, NOT vector-pinned. CROSS-CORE BOUNDARY (this u64 fix): the >=2^64 reject family is pinned as uvarint_overflow and MUST agree byte-for-byte across go/rs/ts -- uvarint_overflow_ge_2_64 (11-byte LEB128 reaching the 2^64 boundary), uvarint_overflow_11_continuation_bytes (11 continuation bytes, no terminator: shift passes the 64-bit ceiling), uvarint_overflow_11byte_canonical (11-byte shortest-form uvarint; a canonical u64 uvarint is at most 10 bytes, so any 11-byte uvarint necessarily encodes >=2^64). These three are pinned because all three cores detect overflow STRUCTURALLY via the continuation/length ceiling, independent of value-wrapping; they are unambiguous cross-core. A 10-byte input whose 10th terminating byte alone pushes the value over 2^64 (e.g. 00ffffffffffffffffff7f) is INTENTIONALLY NOT pinned: cores that compute the value in wrapped 64-bit arithmetic re-encode the wrapped result and report non_canonical_uvarint, while a full-precision core reports uvarint_overflow -- they disagree, so that shape is not a stable cross-core vector. DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED EITHER: the valid-u64-but-too-large boundary -- a uvarint that IS a valid u64 (e.g. 2^64-1 = uvarint ffffffffffffffffff01) but exceeds a core's native MATERIALIZATION width. Per spec §3.1 that is an implementation-local RESOURCE LIMIT (limit_exceeded class), NOT uvarint_overflow, and each core tests its own boundary in its own suite (Go: > maxInt = 2^63-1; Rust: only triggers on 32-bit usize targets; TS: > Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 2^53-1).
